title: Publish privacy policy & DPA
summary: Stand up the privacy paperwork customers ask for: generate the privacy policy and terms, get counsel review, publish to the site, and wire a DPA signature flow with a maintained subprocessor list.

parts.title: Generate privacy policy and terms
parts.guidance: Map personal information collected through the product, billing, support, analytics and AI features: its source, purpose, recipients, retention and user controls. Draft the privacy notice from those facts and the terms from the service’s commercial behavior. Resolve unknown behavior with the people maintaining the relevant systems. Identify legal-basis and territorial questions for the legal review.

options.title: Default — Generate privacy policy and terms
options.summary: Draft from verified collection points, purposes, recipients, retention, user controls and company contact details. Keep commercial terms separate from the privacy notice so each can be reviewed against its own promises. Reuse approved language only where it still describes the product. Mark unknown facts for their system owners and unresolved legal content for the review step.

options.title: India - DPDP Act 2023
options.summary: Map the Indian user interactions, collected data, purposes and responsible entity. For the legal review, compare those facts with the DPDP Act, published Rules, corrigendum and enforcement timeline. Separate provisions already in force from later commencement before choosing notice, consent or operational changes. Use that assessment to adapt the Indian notice; a GDPR template does not establish the applicable Indian duties.
options.when: Privacy policy for users in India

options.title: UK - UK GDPR + ICO fee
options.summary: Review the company’s UK processing and role when adapting the notice. Use the ICO fee guidance to assess payment requirements and exemptions separately from the notice itself. If payment is due, the authorized company representative registers and approves payment. Keep the assessment and any receipt with the UK privacy records so policy publication is not mistaken for completing the fee obligation.
options.when: Privacy policy for users in the United Kingdom

options.title: Germany - GDPR + BDSG specifics
options.summary: Assess the German processing activities against GDPR and BDSG section 38 DPO triggers. Consider processing activities and the staff involved, including triggers that apply independently of headcount. Resolve the appointment decision in the legal review, then align contact details and escalation responsibilities with it. Keep the basis for the decision so changes in processing or staffing can prompt reassessment.
options.when: Privacy policy for users in Germany

options.title: France - CNIL cookie rules
options.summary: Inventory cookies, SDKs and other trackers, including what loads before a visitor makes a choice. Check their purposes and claimed exemptions against the current CNIL materials. Test acceptance, refusal and withdrawal in the actual service, then make the notice describe that behavior. Keep the tracker list and test evidence together so later analytics changes can be checked against the same consent setup.
options.when: Privacy policy for users in France

parts.title: Review with counsel
parts.guidance: Review the drafts with counsel alongside data flows, customer types, target markets and existing contracts. Highlight sensitive data, children’s use, transfers, analytics and any mismatch between the text and product behavior. Resolve both wording changes and operational changes needed to support the promises. Identify who will implement each unresolved change before the reviewed documents are published.

parts.title: Publish policies to the website
parts.guidance: Release the approved policies at their intended website and product locations. Verify footer and signup links, mobile rendering, contact details and the displayed version. Check that the live wording matches the reviewed document and that any required consent or acknowledgement flow points to it. Keep the published version available to support and preserve its release history for later questions.

parts.title: Set up the DPA e-signature flow
parts.guidance: Populate the approved DPA with the correct contracting parties, service description and processing schedules. Check whether the customer contract already incorporates it and route requested changes to the legal reviewer. Send the approved agreement to verified signers in the agreed signature order. Link the executed agreement and signature evidence to the customer; an invitation or template link is still pending.

parts.title: Maintain the subprocessor list
parts.guidance: Reconcile the subprocessor list with engineering and procurement records. For each service, verify the legal entity, processing purpose, locations and relevant contract. Review proposed additions against customer notice or objection commitments before changing the public list. Preserve previous versions and completed notices so the privacy owner can explain which processors were disclosed and when.

geoNotes.summary: The Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023 is the GDPR analog: consent-first processing, notice requirements and data-fiduciary duties, with rules phasing in — privacy paper for India cites the DPDP Act, not the GDPR.
UK GDPR applies post-Brexit with the ICO as regulator — and there is a concrete registration step US startups miss: nearly every data-processing company must pay the ICO's annual data protection fee.

GDPR plus the BDSG: German specifics include mandatory data protection officers at lower thresholds (generally 20+ people regularly processing personal data) and enforcement by strict state DPAs alongside the federal BfDI.

The CNIL is Europe's most active enforcer of GDPR cookie/consent rules — its published guidelines on cookies and trackers are effectively the spec for a French-market privacy policy and consent banner.

metadata.supportReason: Policy generation, site publishing, and DPA signature routing are automatable. Counsel review is judgment work you should not skip.
